# Pippa and the Borrowed Star

<!-- Generated by story export. -->

# Chapter 1: The Clock That Sneezed

It was Christmas Eve. Dusk turned the snow pink and blue.

Pippa Wrenmouse lived behind the gears of the Old Clock Tower. She was tiny and grey, with a red thread scarf and a tool belt that jingled when she walked.

Tonight she dusted the low gears with her feather brush. Swish, swish. The air smelled of warm oil and cocoa.

Pippa never went past the third gear. It sat too high. Her tummy flipped just to look at it.

"Ooh!" she whispered. A pale moth fluttered past her nose, soft as powder.

She pattered after it. Tip tap, tip tap went her feet on the cold brass.

"Oops-sorry!" she said when her brush tickled the big spring by mistake.

The moth landed on the clock nose wheel. Pippa reached up with her brush. Tickle, tickle.

The whole tower breathed in deep.

Then it sneezed. "A-CHOO!"

The gears shivered. The chains swung. Pippa grabbed her scarf and sat down with a plop.

High above, the Borrowed Star wobbled in its nest. It was small as a pinecone, peach-gold and warm. Every night it lit Tinsel Hollow.

Now it tipped. It rolled. It fell soft as a feather down into the snow. Poof!

Pippa peeked over the low ledge. Her heart thumped fast.

Down in the village, lamp after lamp turned sleepy blue. The light yawned and grew dim.

Pippa felt sorry and soft inside. She had not meant to make such a big sneeze.

"Are you all right, Star?" she asked in a small voice.

She scampered down the tower stairs. The snow went crunch, crunch under her boots. It smelled clean and cold.

At the bottom, something glowed in a dip in the snow. A warm peach-gold glow.

Pippa gasped. Then she remembered the empty jam jar she had saved under her workbench. Old Tobias Clockkeeper had poked star holes in the lid for her, just for fun.

She ran to fetch it. Her scarf flapped behind her.

The glow pulsed soft and slow behind her, like it was calling her to come and see.

# Chapter 2: A Jar for a Star

Pippa knelt in the snow by the warm glow. Her whiskers trembled.

"Quick-quick!" called a voice from the sky. Wrenna Sparrow swooped down with a swish of brown wings. Snow puffed up around her feet.

"Ooh!" said Pippa. "The Star fell down. It went poof, and now it glows."

Wrenna bent to peek close beside her. The Borrowed Star lay in the snow, small as a pinecone and peach-gold all over. It pulsed soft and sleepy.

Just then Bram Tinker-Mole huffed up the hill. He was round and slow, with snow on his nose and a warm dough cloth in his paws. He smelled like fresh bread.

"Slow and steady," said Bram. "I brought something soft. For carrying stars."

Old Tobias Clockkeeper came next, in his long coat, with kind eyes. He carried the jam jar lid with star holes. Pippa had left the jar by the door in her hurry.

"Thank you, little one," said Tobias. "You saved just what we need."

Together they scooped. Bram slid the dough cloth under the Star. Wrenna lifted gentle, gentle with her beak. Pippa held the jam jar wide. Plip! In went the Star, warm and glowing.

Pippa sang a tiny thank-you song. The glow grew still and steady.

Tobias knelt low beside her. "Stars borrow their light," he said. "This one fell, and now it must rest. Before dawn, it must sleep in the Stone Nest atop the Wishing Pine on Starberry Hill. Keep it warm. Hold it in turns. Sing to it."

Pippa lifted the jar all by herself. Oof! It was too heavy. Her arms wobbled.

Bram smiled. "Slow and steady is better with friends," he said.

Pippa unwound her red thread scarf from her neck. They tied it into a sling, so each friend could take a turn.

Then Tobias pressed a wobbly brass button into her paw. "For luck, little one," he said.

Granny Nutmeg the hedgehog bustled up with her basket. The air smelled of cinnamon and honey. "My dears," she said. "You look cold. Take two." She gave each of them a warm courage bun.

Pippa took a nibble. Crunchy top, soft middle. Yum.

Tobias looked at the sleepy blue lamps of Tinsel Hollow. Then he looked east, where morning would come.

"We have till morning light," he said.

# Chapter 3: Through Tinsel Hollow

The snow squeaked under Pippa's boots. The village was dark around her, but not scary dark. The lamps glowed sleepy blue, like eyes half closed. Pippa held the jam jar close to her chest. Inside, the Star gave a small sleepy blink.

Bram walked beside her. His big feet went crunch, crunch. "Slow and steady," he said. His pockets jingled with snacks. Wrenna fluttered low over their heads. "Quick-quick! No ice this way!" she called. Old Tobias came at the back with his lantern stick. The Star light wobbled in the jar.

Pippa stopped at Granny Nutmeg's door. Her tummy felt fluttery. She had practiced asking all the way down the lane. "Please, can we... please, may we..." Her voice came out tiny. Bram gave her a soft nudge. Old Tobias bent low beside her. "Go on, little one," he hummed. She knocked tap, tap, tap. "Oops-sorry!" she squeaked, even before anyone answered.

The door opened with a warm creak. Light spilled out like honey. Granny Nutmeg stood there in her patchwork shawl. She had hurried home ahead with her basket. "Why, my dears!" she said. "Come in from the cold." Pippa held the jar up high. "Ooh!" Granny said softly when she saw the Star. Pippa found her big voice deep down. "Please, may we share a little flame to keep it warm?"

Granny Nutmeg lit an extra candle. "Take two," she said. She tucked a second warm bun into Bram's pocket too. Next door, the Badger twins opened their shutters. Then Mole Mama opened hers. Then old Finch opened his. They shared a flame from one to the next. Soon a string of golden lights bobbed down Tinsel Hollow. Someone started the walking-song. "Share a spark, carry it far." Pippa sang too, soft at first. Then she sang louder. Near the shared candles, the Star stretched. It glowed brighter. Pippa felt warm right down to her toes. "Thank you," she whispered. The light grew steady.

The friends stopped at the end of the lane. Starberry Hill loomed tall and white above them. Wrenna landed low on Bram's hat. "Quick-quick! Path is clear to the foot!" she peeped. A little soup pot steamed there under a crooked pine. The smell of carrots and warm bread curled into the cold air. Pippa breathed it in deep. "Ooh!" she said.

# Chapter 4: The Slippery Hill

The wind found them at the bottom of Starberry Hill. It tugged Pippa's ears and made the snow hiss. The path up was white and slippery. Pippa took one step. Slip. She took one more. Slide. "Ooh!" she said. "It is so steep." High above, the Wishing Pine swayed at the very top.

Halfway up, the Star in the jar flickered. Its light went thin and wobbly, like a candle in wind. Pippa cupped her paws around the jar. "Please stay," she whispered. The light sank lower. Her own legs felt wobbly too. "I want to go back down," she said in a small voice.

Bram knelt down fast. "Slow and steady," he said. He opened his big coat like a cape and wrapped it round Pippa and the jar. Old Tobias leaned in close. "Easy, little one," he said. He hummed their walking-song, low and soft. Wrenna swooped low. "Quick-quick! I see mouse-steps! Zig and zag!" she cried. The wind still pushed, but inside the coat-cape it was warm and still.

Pippa remembered the saved courage bun in Bram's snack pocket. Her paws shook as she broke it in half. "One for you, Bram. One for me. Courage buns," she said. She nibbled and felt a little braver. "Thank you for waiting for me," she told the Star. "Thank you for keeping me warm," she told her friends. "Oops-sorry I am so slow," she added. The Star gave a warm pink glow. Its light steadied and grew. Bram smiled. "Brave is asking when you need help," he said.

They rested in the hollow of Pippa's scarf-sling. Pippa held the jar and sang a tiny thank-you song till her ears stopped trembling. The Star rested too, tucked warm in moss and wool. Its glow held steady and kind. Then she looked up. The Wishing Pine towered over them. Its top swayed in the dark sky. Pippa's tummy flipped. She was afraid of heights. "Ooh," she gulped. "All the way up there?"

# Chapter 5: Up the Wishing Pine

Pippa tipped her head back and looked up. Up. Up.

The Wishing Pine rose tall over her, kind and wide. Its bark smelled like snow and pine sap. Ribbons fluttered from its lower branches, tied there long ago for wishes. Near the very top, tucked where the branches grew close, sat the Stone Nest. It was round and empty and waiting.

"Only small paws can climb that high," Old Tobias said, soft. "The branches grow too close for big hands."

Pippa's knees wobbled. She squeezed the wobbly button on her coat. Squeeze, squeeze.

"I knocked it down," she whispered. "So I'll carry it back. Even if my knees wobble."

Bram tied his ladder-string firm around the lowest branch and held it steady with both paws. "Slow and steady," he rumbled. "I have got the string. You have got the star."

Wrenna landed light on a low branch and tapped it with her foot. "Quick-quick! This way, Pippa! Paw here, then here!"

Pippa tucked the jam-jar close, where the little star rested warm in moss. She set one paw on the string. Then the bark. Then up.

Branch by branch, her friends talked her up.

"Paw left," said Bram from below.

"Good! Now right! Quick-quick, you did it!" said Wrenna from just above.

Halfway up, Pippa's tail trembled. Below her, lights began to bloom in the dark. The village had followed all the way up the hill. Lamp after lamp lifted high. Tobias held his lantern. Nutmeg held her bakery candle. Then Pippa heard a hum. It was low and sweet and rising, like soup warming.

They were humming her star song.

Pippa squeezed her button again. "Brave is asking for help," she whispered. "And I asked."

So she climbed, scared anyway. Up past the ribbons. Up past the last pinecone. Up until her nose touched the cold stone of the Stone Nest.

Pippa breathed out slow and soft. She lifted the jam-jar and set it gently in the middle of the nest. She unscrewed the lid.

Inside, the little star shivered.

It sipped the cold night air. It sipped the pine smell and the song still rising from below.

Then it shivered once more... and glowed.

# Chapter 6: Morning Light

For a moment nothing moved.

Then the little star stretched. It twinkled once, soft as a yawn. A thin line of pink light spilled over Starberry Hill. Morning was coming.

Pippa held her breath. The star lifted out of the jam-jar, light as milkweed down. It hovered by her cheek, warm as a thank you. Then it floated up. Up past the ribbons. Up past Wrenna circling slow to guide it. Up until it found its place in the paling sky and settled there with a happy blink.

Below, every lamp bloomed brighter, as if the village lights had taken a deep sip too. The hum rose into a soft cheer.

Pippa climbed down into waiting arms. Bram caught her with a soft oof and held the ladder-string steady till both her feet touched snow. "Slow and steady," he said. "I have you." Nutmeg wrapped her in a warm shawl and said, "my dears." Wrenna bumped her cheek with a wing and whispered, "Quick-quick! You did it!"

Pippa looked up at the sky. "I am sorry I knocked you down," she whispered. The star twinkled back, kind and rested. Tobias laid a big warm hand near her and said, "Stars borrow their light, Pippa. So must we. You shared it well."

Her knees still wobbled. But her heart felt warm and full. She had not been brave alone. She had been brave together.

By sunrise they were all back at the bakery for Christmas morning. The oven glowed. The table held barley soup with steam curling up and honey buns with melted tops. Pippa told how the star had sipped song and thanks and rest. Nutmeg nodded and said, "Then every year, my dears, we will share soup and light on this day." And just like that the Share-Light Supper was born.

Pippa lifted her cup. "I wish for warm homes and shared light," she said. "Thank you, Bram. Thank you, Wrenna. Thank you, Tobias. Thank you, Nutmeg."

Up in the tower, Tobias wound the old clock. It ticked happy and true.

That night Pippa curled sleepy-safe in her nook under Gear Three, button held loose in one paw, while her star winked softly through the window.
